layout_map:
1. Header strip: solid purple band across the top containing the slide title ("Quadratic Kernel Mapping and Kernel Trick") left-of-center and a yellow circular slide-number chip ("26") at the top-right corner.
2. Top formula band: light cream panel with vector definitions (a = [a₁; a₂], b = [b₁; b₂]) and the boxed expansion of (aᵀb)².
3. Middle formula band: feature-map derivation φ(a)ᵀφ(b) with the column vector φ(x), a right-side target column vector, and the red "2D → 3D" annotation beneath.
4. Bottom formula band: numeric instantiation with a = [1; 2], b = [3; 4], the expanded dot product, intermediate vectors, the sum "9 + 64 + 48 = 121", and the final equality "[aᵀb]² = (1·3 + 2·4)² = 11² = 121" with a right-pointing red arrow and return glyph.
5. Right annotation edge: red callout arrows and equality markers running along the right side of the formula bands.
6. Outer frame: thin gray border enclosing the full slide with rounded corners on a cream background fill.
first_glance_test: Within 3 seconds a viewer understands this is a math lecture slide about kernel mapping; the saturated purple title header wins the eye immediately. Apparent actions are passive consumption only: read the derivation, follow the 2D → 3D feature mapping, and verify the numeric example — all three stages are visible at first glance with nothing hidden behind hover or collapse. Given the VIEW purpose (lecture frame), the focal point should be the central derivation; it commands attention by central placement and scale, though the bold header competes nearly equally.
strengths: Saturated purple header establishes document identity and slide number instantly (top header strip).
Three-band vertical stack cleanly separates theory, feature-space mapping, and numeric verification, guiding the eye downward (full composition).
Color-coded mathematical symbols (red/blue/green) make variable tracking easy across the derivation (all formula bands).

defects.description: bottom formula band — final equality line — the "↵" return-glyph chip beside "121" reads as keyboard/UI residue rather than mathematical notation — replace with a standard math marker or remove.

top_3: [minor|med] bottom formula band — final equality line — return-glyph residue reads as keyboard artifact in a math derivation — see §4 (b).
structural_proposal:
1. Move the red "2D → 3D" label into the middle formula band as a run-in section header so the dimensionality claim is anchored to the φ(x) definition rather than floating between bands (source: middle band, below vector equation → destination: middle band, above vector equation).
2. [out-of-scope] dock this slide into the dark app shell as a help/reference pane; no app navigation or shell is visible on screen to integrate against.
uncertainties: The injected context describes a dark-themed parent app, but the capture is a light-themed lecture slide; I judged the slide on its own merits and cannot determine if it lives inside an app shell.
Subscript glyphs (a₁, b₂, x₁, etc.) sit near the legibility floor at 1× capture but appear readable; I did not guess at any content.
Whether the red return glyph (↵) is intentional notation or an artifact cannot be verified from a static image; flagged as a low-confidence suspicion.
